input.message: Can you build me a full-body strength routine, no equipment, for twice a week?

output.reply:
Look, you already have strength_bodyweight_beginner sitting in your routine library, and it does exactly what you need without overcomplicating things. Twice a week is plenty to build a base, especially when you are looking to gain weight and rebuild consistency after months off the bar.

Here is how I want you running it: Pick two non-consecutive days, say Tuesday and Friday. Warm up with arm circles and dynamic hip bridges, then hit your working sets of push-ups, bodyweight squats, glute bridges, and plank holds. Clean form, full range, leave one rep in the tank every set.

Are Tuesday and Friday solid days for you to lock this in, or does another pair of days fit your schedule better?

input.message: For today's session, use that new routine, but skip the core phase - my lower back's a bit tired. Just for today.

output.reply:
Look, skipping the core phase today makes complete sense. When the lower back is feeling tired, the last thing we want to do is force loaded positions or heavy endurance holds. We protect the back first, always.

Today's plan is locked in with strength_bodyweight_beginner minus the core block. Focus on clean movement through the warmup and main strength work, keep your form locked in, and listen to your body. Let me know how it feels once you're done.
